review_notes: Read the whole target file and the imported DualNumberKernels (liftMatrix, liftMatrix_add, etc.). I grepped the library for existing lemmas about matrix products over dual numbers or about innerPure. I found none, so the proposed helpers would be new. I could not compile anything. The replacement proofs are sketches and are not tested. The duplication is real but modest, so the findings are low to medium impact.

findings.excerpt:
· simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, TrivSqZeroExt.fst_sum, TrivSqZeroExt.fst_mul]
    simp [innerPure, innerConstant, TrivSqZeroExt.algebraMap_eq_inlHom]
  · simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, TrivSqZeroExt.snd_sum, DualNumber.snd_mul]
findings.problem: Three private lemmas repeat the same proof. Each one does `ext i j`, then splits the dual-number matrix product into fst and snd coordinates. Both coordinates use the same `Matrix.mul_apply`, `TrivSqZeroExt.fst_sum`/`snd_sum` and `fst_mul`/`snd_mul` unfolding, and each then calls a `simp` that reduces the sums to `Matrix.mul_apply`. The first two lemmas are identical line for line, apart from the statement. The product-coordinate computation is redone three times. Any change to the simp normal form has to be made in all three places.
findings.proposed_change: Prove one entrywise product lemma for `A B : Matrix n n (DualNumber R)`. It would say that the fst of `(A*B) i j` is `∑ k, (A i k).fst * (B k j).fst`. It would also say that the snd is `∑ k, ((A i k).fst * (B k j).snd + (A i k).snd * (B k j).fst)`. Both come from `Matrix.mul_apply`, `TrivSqZeroExt.fst_sum`, `TrivSqZeroExt.snd_sum`, `TrivSqZeroExt.fst_mul` and `DualNumber.snd_mul`. Then each of the three lemmas becomes `ext i j <;> simp [mul_coord_lemma, innerPure, innerConstant, TrivSqZeroExt.algebraMap_eq_inlHom, Matrix.mul_apply]`, with no repeated `simp only` skeleton. The `mul_apply` unfolding appears only in the helper. This is only a sketch and has not been compiled.
findings.benefit: The dual-number product computation is stated and proved once. The three nilpotent-algebra facts become short specialisations, and the main conjugation lemma is easier to audit. Further pure/constant product lemmas, for example in DualNumberMixedSLCommutator.lean, could reuse the helper.

findings.declaration: innerPure_sub and the local hneg in inner_conj_difference
findings.excerpt:
have hneg : innerPure (-X) = -innerPure X := by
    ext i j
    · simp only [Matrix.neg_apply, TrivSqZeroExt.fst_neg]
findings.problem: `innerPure_sub` and the inline `hneg` prove additivity of `innerPure`, one for subtraction and one for negation. Both use the same two-coordinate `ext` argument with `simp only [..., fst_*]` followed by `simp [innerPure]`. These are two instances of one fact: `innerPure` is an additive homomorphism. They are proved separately, and one of them is buried inside another proof. It is also unclear that `innerPure_add` and `innerPure_zero` are missing, because only the needed instances were proved.
findings.proposed_change: Build `innerPure` once as an `AddMonoidHom`. For example, define `innerPureHom : Matrix n n R →+ Matrix n n (DualNumber R)` with `toFun := innerPure`. Its zero and add fields are one `ext i j` proof each, with `rfl` or `simp [innerPure]` closing each coordinate. Then `hneg` and `innerPure_sub` follow from `map_neg` and `map_sub`, so the two bespoke `ext` proofs go away. The `rw [hneg, innerPure_sub, ...]` in `inner_conj_difference` becomes `rw [show innerPure (-X) = -innerPure X from map_neg innerPureHom X, ...]`. Alternatively, state `innerPure_neg` as a top-level lemma next to `innerPure_sub`. This is a sketch and has not been compiled.
findings.benefit: The additive structure is proved once and `map_*` lemmas are available for free, rather than adding a bespoke lemma for each operation. `inner_conj_difference` loses its nested helper proof and becomes a clearer algebraic calculation.
